result.title: Procedural Memory for Language Agents: A Neurosymbolic Perspective on Explicit Goal Structure
result.summary: Large language models remain unreliable on long-horizon tasks requiring procedural reasoning. We argue that a key cause is the absence of explicit procedural memory: accessible, modifiable knowledge of how tasks are accomplished, distinct from semantic and episodic memory. Goal-Oriented Graphs offer such a representation, encoding goals and prerequisite dependencies as inspectable symbolic structure. We examine their construction, the challenges they pose, and principles for integrating them with neural reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张 LLM 在长时程程序性推理上不可靠源于缺少显式的程序性记忆，提出以 Goal-Oriented Graphs 将目标与前置依赖编码为可检视的符号结构，并讨论其构建难点及与神经推理的整合原则。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是面向纯文本 agent 的显式程序性知识与目标依赖表示，可为核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要结构、以及前置依赖式监督与状态可修改性提供方法线索；但无视觉/多模态证据，与主线联系需进一步核查。
